title: Rollout Orchestrator: Signal Aggregation & Trace Bridge for Variant Health
creator: Priya Kapoor
description:
Goal: Build a console-first Rollout Orchestrator feature set that aggregates signal streams (latency, error rate, token cost, semantic drift) across variants and ties them to traces and per-route telemetry. Deliver a single-pane Variant Health view with a Trace Bridge that can surface sampled traces linked to rollout deltas and allow operators to pivot between A/B, canary, and shadow traffic comparisons.

Background: Customers currently use separate dashboards and traces to investigate rollout regressions. This creates a slow feedback loop during canary and A/B experiments. The Orchestrator will combine time-aligned aggregated metrics, divergence summaries, and trace snippets so operators can make faster rollout decisions and optionally trigger auto-rollback.

Scope: Console UI components and backend telemetry aggregation pipeline only. Not in scope: changes to serving runtime scheduling or new model variants. Scope details:
- Aggregation: rollup token-level cost, p95/p50 latency, top-3 error fingerprints, and semantic divergence score per-variant and per-route.
- Trace Bridge: follow a request from aggregate metric spike to N sampled traces (client request -> route -> model variant) and show KV-cache hit/miss annotations and batch size.
- Diff Views: side-by-side delta visualization for any two variants or time windows; supports A/B splits and shadow vs live.
- Auto-rollback integration: pluggable policy rules (thresholds, evaluation windows, cooldown). When enabled, Orchestrator emits a decision event to the deployment service.

Acceptance criteria:
1) Console shows Variant Health for a selected route within 5s of selection and renders diff overlays for two variants.
2) Trace Bridge returns 3 sample traces correlated with the metric spike and annotates per-step metadata.
3) Aggregated metrics align with existing per-route dashboards within a 3% margin on p95 and error rate.
4) Auto-rollback rules can be created in the UI and successfully fire a dry-run decision against staging deployment without mutating production.

Key trade-offs and decisions we debated:
- Sampling vs full tracing: initial launch will use adaptive sampling to bound storage and latency; plan to tune sampling weight for rollout traffic.
- Aggregation window: 1m buckets provide fast feedback but increase noise; default to 1m with 5m smoothing option.
- Diff visualization: lightweight statistical summary vs full distribution plotting; we will ship summary + small sparkline and add full distributions in follow-ups.

Telemetry and metrics to track post-launch:
- Time-to-insight: median time from alert to a trace being surfaced.
- Precision of rollback triggers: percent of dry-run rollbacks that would have prevented a degraded SLO.
- Console latency: 95th percentile time to render Variant Health UI.

Notes for engineering: backend requires a rolling-join between metric aggregates and sampled trace index keyed by route+variant+time. Keep join window configurable. Provide an API for the console to request aligned metrics and traces.
acceptance_criteria: 1) Variant Health UI renders for selected route with two-variant diff in <5s; 2) Trace Bridge returns 3 representative traces annotated with KV/cache/batch info; 3) Aggregated metrics match per-route dashboards within 3%; 4) Auto-rollback dry-run can be executed from UI without changing production deployments.
comments: 2026-02-22 - Priya K.: Kickoff meeting with Eng and Design. Agreed to MVP scope: aggregation, trace bridge, simple diffs, auto-rollback dry-run only.

2026-02-26 - Ethan M.: Spike complete. Prototype shows adaptive sampling plus a small index for sampled traces. Backend needs a high-cardinality join strategy; proposing pre-aggregated keys at route+variant+bucket.
2026-03-02 - Lina Torres (Design): Initial mockups uploaded to Figma. Emphasis on quick signal triage: heatbar for error spikes, and a stacked cost/latency view.
2026-03-05 - Security review request filed (ENG-9102). Security flagged data retention of traces; recommend 30d retention for rollout traces by default and 90d for enterprise plan.

2026-03-08 - Infra note from Marcus O.: We should cap trace fetch to 250KB payloads for console requests to keep UI fast. Backend will return a short summary if traces exceed budget with a link to raw trace archive.
2026-03-10 - Priya K.: Scope locked for Cycle 2026-W09. Moving to implementation. Design and backend tasks split into tickets and assigned to ENG-8841, ENG-8842, ENG-8849.
